name: Victor Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal shift look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and have answered calls and chats about parcel deliveries for years. I finished secondary school and can handle most claims, though I still ask a senior agent about unusual credits. I use approved AI search now and then after a colleague shows me the source. I like settling a missing parcel; I dislike having the same wrong address bounce back tomorrow.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does your pay need to cover at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife sews alterations from home, with uneven orders. We have a mortgage and two school-age children, seven and twelve. My pay is low for this work, we have less than one month saved, and there are few other centres nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my shift a faster draft is welcome if an agent still checks the address. A wrong parcel promise comes back as a second call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have handled deliveries for years and know most of the routine, so I don't fear a small tool. What frightens me is our mortgage with less than a month's expenses saved and this lower pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep my delivery calls and use the approved search tool now and then, checking the original order. Starting this payday, my wife and I will stop the bought lunches on our workdays and put the saved money aside through the first year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about bills, fairly steady at work. The bank account doesn't become safer just because the software stops improving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is your wife's income like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My wife sews alterations from home, and some weeks are busy while others are bare. Our children are seven and twelve, so both school and house bills arrive whether her orders do or not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When do you use the search tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I used an old answer once and missed a changed delivery rule. Since then I ask a colleague to show me the proof before using a new tool for that kind of case.

say: I'd welcome a **faster draft** only when agents check addresses.
I'd warn a **wrong promise** becomes another customer call.
think: I expect my **experienced role** to continue in a mild change.
I fear our **mortgage gap** because low pay and under a month saved leave little room.
do: Keep handling **delivery calls** and checking original orders.
Use the **approved search tool** only on proved case types.
Stop **bought lunches** and save the cost from this payday.
feel: **Anxious** about bills, though work feels steady.
S0.quote: The bank account doesn't become safer just because the software stops improving.
fieldNote: His **call experience** gives confidence in the work, not the budget.
His wife's **alteration orders** make the second income variable.
He uses **AI occasionally** after a colleague proves the relevant case.

steps.text: Keep taking delivery calls and checking original order records
Save the cost of workday lunches from each payday

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the centre should show us which delivery chats it plans to automate and which shifts remain paid. If the new reply tool is required, I want a real test first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Much of my day is checking addresses and answering repeat questions, so my hours could fall. A long job search would put the mortgage behind quickly; there are few other centres nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll ask for a week of repeat-call figures and test the new reply tool on ten closed cases only if it becomes standard and I get paid practice time. If my hours fall in the first year, I'll apply for a posted paid stock clerk job at the local building supplier only if its hours and wage cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I've seen this floor run lean before, and a thin reserve won't let us wait it out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What figures would you bring?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd bring the repeated-address cases to my supervisor with the numbers written down. A claim about saved minutes is no good if three customers call back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would you change jobs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The supplier job must be real and paid, with steady enough hours for the house. I won't quit the centre for a trial week without wages.

say: I'd request **paid-shift numbers** before delivery chats move.
I'd ask for a **real test** if the reply tool becomes standard.
think: I expect my **address-checking hours** could shrink.
I cannot carry a **long search** with few nearby centres and almost no savings.
do: Test **ten closed cases** only with paid time if the tool becomes standard.
Bring **repeat-call figures** to my supervisor this month.
Apply for **posted paid stock work** after cuts only if wages and hours cover mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about hours and a thin household reserve.
S1.quote: A claim about saved minutes is no good if three customers call back.
fieldNote: His **routine screen tasks** expose a long-held job to early change.
He needs **paid practice** before a compulsory tool touches claims.
He requires a **real supplier vacancy** with mortgage-covering hours.

steps.text: Test ten closed reply cases on paid time if tool becomes standard
Apply for posted paid stock work after cuts only if wages and hours cover mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues general AI by 2028 could handle our calls before a new rota is ready. Robots around 2031 are later for physical work, not a delay for headsets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my delivery calls could disappear, even after years of doing them. My wife's sewing income cannot carry the mortgage and two children alone, and our savings are under one month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Today I'll gather our mortgage figures and ask for written notice dates. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I'll apply for posted paid stock jobs with hours and wages covering the mortgage, and ask my father about one payment only after checking which bill is short and whether he can spare it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, and I would not sleep easily. I can make calls, but I cannot earn a new wage just by asking for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you cut first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my wife the first cut would be the planned family trip. The children can still have weekends together without buying tickets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can your father cover the gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My father has his own household to pay for, so I would not count on him. I would ask about one mortgage payment only if the due date comes before another wage.

say: I'd warn **2028 general AI** could answer our calls.
I'd explain **2031 robots** do not extend telephone work.
think: I expect my **delivery job** could end.
I know my wife's **sewing income** cannot cover our mortgage and children alone.
do: Ask for **written notice** and check mortgage figures today.
Apply for **posted paid stock jobs** after a real cut only if wages and hours cover mortgage.
Ask my **father for one payment** only after confirming the shortfall and his ability to help.
feel: **Alarmed** about losing the wage with almost no reserve.
S2.quote: My wife's sewing income cannot carry the mortgage and two children alone, and our savings are under one month.
fieldNote: He knows **years of service** do not stop broad call automation.
He treats **fatherly help** as uncertain and limited to one actual shortfall.
His first **spending cut** is a family trip, not school needs.

steps.text: Apply for posted paid stock jobs after cuts only if wages and hours cover mortgage
Ask father for one mortgage payment only after checking shortfall and availability
Cancel planned family trip if his call wage stops
Gather mortgage figures and request written notice before applying for stock jobs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is time to show which jobs are actually paid and which classes they need. Thinking AI reaches our calls in 2031, and hands-on robots come around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build a route into stock work if the supplier has a real vacancy. I know the physical work could change after robots arrive, so I won't spend mortgage money on a course without a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my call shift and ask the building supplier about a paid trial day. If it posts a paid stock role with bill-covering hours and covers the required safety course, I'll complete that course on paid time; in the first year after 2031, I'll move only for a written offer that still covers our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can check a real shift. Five years gives me more than an advert to judge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a full trial show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask what a full delivery day weighs and when the crew starts. Lifting stock for a neighbour once is not the same as being paid all week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What other costs would you check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my wife to compare the new rota with her sewing orders and the children's school pickup. If the job leaves us paying for extra care, its wage must cover that too.

say: I'd seek **real paid roles** during the five-year window.
I'd say **2034 robots** follow our 2031 call risk.
think: I might move into **stock work** with a real opening.
I won't spend **mortgage money** on training for an unposted job.
do: Keep my **call shift** while it pays.
Complete **funded safety course** on paid time only for a posted role with mortgage-covering wages and hours.
Move after 2031 only for a **written offer** whose wages and hours cover mortgage and extra care.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to inspect a paid day first.
S3.quote: Lifting stock for a neighbour once is not the same as being paid all week.
fieldNote: He checks **lifting and start time** before treating stock work as income.
His **course path** requires a posted paid role and covered training.
The **childcare cost** must fit the written wage too.

steps.text: Keep working paid delivery calls while shifts remain
Complete funded course on paid time only for posted stock role with mortgage-covering wages and hours
Move only on written paid offer whose hours and wages cover mortgage and extra care
Ask for a paid supplier trial day and inspect lifting and start times

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the centre a decade gives us time to show real staffing numbers and let people test paid work elsewhere. Our phones face general AI in 2036; hands-on robots arrive around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 the children may be older, but the mortgage may remain. I could keep serving customers for years, yet a long warning doesn't make our current savings any thicker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep my calls and move a fixed sum from each payday into the house account. I'll check posted supplier jobs each year; in the first year after 2036, if my call hours fall, I'll apply only for a written paid offer with steady hours and wages covering the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the distant change and anxious about this month's bills. I can build the reserve slowly if the work stays full.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the children to look for a paid place to learn before buying a course. A title is not a household wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much could you save?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My target is three months of expenses, but if sewing orders fall, we'll take longer. I won't call an empty bank account a plan.

say: I'd ask for **real staffing numbers** over the decade, including paid hours rather than just calls answered.
I'd distinguish **2036 calls** from robots around 2039.
think: I might still owe on the **mortgage at 53**.
I know a **long warning** does not fix today's thin savings.
do: Keep my **call job** while shifts stay full.
Save a **fixed sum** toward three months of expenses if wages allow.
Apply after 2036 only after **call-hour cuts** and for written paid stock offers with steady hours and mortgage-covering wages.
feel: **Uneasy** about future work and anxious about current bills.
S4.quote: A title is not a household wage.
fieldNote: His **three-month target** depends on wages and sewing orders staying available.
He asks for **posted work** rather than leaving on a forecast.
Present **mortgage strain** keeps the long scenario anxious.

steps.text: Keep taking paid delivery calls while shifts remain full
Save fixed payday amounts toward three months if wages allow
Apply after call cuts only for written paid stock offers with steady hours and mortgage-covering wages

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. It could end calls before I get a paid stock job, and our mortgage has almost no reserve behind it. Written notice, a posted paid opening and training on paid time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who answers when a parcel is marked delivered but the doorstep is empty. Customers need a person who can look at the address and take responsibility. A faster reply that sends them back tomorrow has solved nothing.

headlineQuote: A faster reply that sends them back tomorrow has solved nothing.
portrait: Victor is an **experienced 43-year-old agent** with secondary schooling and average skill on parcel calls.
He earns **lower pay**, has less than one month saved and faces a mortgage, two schoolchildren and few nearby centres.
His wife's **alteration orders** vary; he uses AI occasionally only when a colleague shows the underlying source.
He seeks **paid stock work** as a conditional bridge while protecting the mortgage from course fees and gaps.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his call wage before another paid shift begins.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** and a posted paid stock opening would give him a plan.
**Paid training time** for a required course would protect the mortgage account.
